in_english.name: Ramin
in_english.long_meaning: Ramin is an Arabic name for a boy, meaning 'witness'. The name is derived from the Arabic word 'Ra'ma' which means 'to see'. The name is often given to a boy who is born after a miscarriage or stillbirth, as a reminder of the previous child that was not seen in this world.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ramin is of Persian origin and is not a common Islamic name. However, the meaning of the name - "one who is kind, gentle and friendly to everyone" - aligns with the Islamic values of kindness, compassion, and love for all of God's creations. Thus, even though the name is not previously used in Islamic circles, its meaning resonates with Islamic teachings and values.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Ramin lies in its reminder of the importance of treating all beings with love and kindness, as taught by Islam. The name encourages the bearer to strive for good character traits and to be a kind and gentle presence in the world. Furthermore, the name Ramin highlights the belief that true spiritual growth comes from treating others with compassion and respect. Ultimately, the name Ramin serves as a daily reminder for its bearer to live a life in accordance with Islamic values of compassion and kindness towards all.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "lover, friend" symbolizes One who is kind, gentle and friendly to everyone.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ramin serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of lover, friend.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 11, Page 199 The name Ramin carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ramin ibn Zalan, a Persian ruler who ruled in Al-Jibal (an area between Damascus and Aleppo) during the Seljuk Empire. He converted to Islam and was appointed as the governor of Baalbek by the Seljuk Sultan.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Kitab Al-Khitat wa-Jughrafiyya, Volume 1, Page 14 The name Ramin carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ramin ibn Ali, a mamluk sultan who ruled Egypt from 1404 to 1406. He was of Circassian origin, but was converted to Islam during his time in Egypt. He overthrew Sultan Al-Nasir Faraj and ruled for a short period before being killed.
